difficulty_reason: After the ordinary Robinson–Schensted and Knuth-equivalence prerequisites, the proof reduces global pattern closure to one-extra-letter Knuth moves and builds explicit obstruction permutations for every non-superstandard hook and two exhaustive nonhook regimes. It controls the deletion of every possible letter using longest-subsequence bounds and detailed insertion/bumping-column constraints. The global classification and its source-local obstruction construction exceed routine qualifying-exam RSK computations; the supporting lemmas and all four author case propositions are retained as uncounted context.
